Q1_seen: Executed finite routing diagnostics and iterative point-to-point ICP/Kabsch trajectories on generated asymmetric 3-D point clouds.
Executed a raw-proxy whole-trajectory split-conformal ablation; its frozen standard run observed 95.83% held-out trajectory coverage and 100% HOLD for all three readers.
Executed the first learned-shape TRAIN=160 / CALIBRATION=160 / FINAL TEST=120 experiment; observed whole-trajectory coverage was 85.00% against a nominal 90% marginal target.

In that first frozen learned test, certificates occurred before estimator stopping in 90.0%, 87.5%, and 87.5% of all assigned episodes for top suction, label alignment, and keyed insertion; overall completion differed by -2.50, -0.83, and 0.00 percentage points; observed unsafe ACT was zero.
Executed a post-review matched same-split comparison on 120 new comparison-test episodes after comparator parameters were frozen from TRAIN/CALIBRATION only.

In the matched comparison, the learned scalar policy stopped earlier than the trajectory-conformal certificate but had more observed unsafe ACTs; for keyed insertion the certificate matched estimator-default completion at 95%, used mean endpoint 11.025 versus 13.100, returned HOLD on 5%, and observed zero unsafe ACT versus estimator-default 5% unsafe ACT.

Executed ten additional reduced-configuration TRAIN=80 / CALIBRATION=80 / TEST=60 cycles with K=16 and 80 points; mean realized coverage was 91.17%, but this is not the same configuration as the first full final test.

GitHub Actions executed the hardened numerical stack, adversarial regressions, matched comparator, lab smoke test, and evidence assertions on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows; the Ubuntu standard-evidence job also completed successfully.
Q2_record_separates: The record separates certificate hitting time from the executed terminal endpoint: no certificate is None/+infinity conceptually, while terminal budget execution may return HOLD.
The record separates latent pose identity from task-reader invariance: multiple retained pose completions can yield one task verdict.
The raw-proxy ablation separates statistical coverage from operational usefulness: a high-coverage envelope can be too wide to license ACT.
The matched comparison separates earliest stopping from coverage/risk-qualified stopping: a scalar threshold can stop earlier while producing more unsafe ACTs.
The record separates trajectory-prefix cost estimates from direct online-policy timing; prefix replay does not license a speed claim.
The first full final-test coverage realization is kept distinct from the reduced-configuration repeated-cycle distribution.
The record does not separate generated-data behavior from real RGB-D/GPU/robot behavior, and marginal conformal coverage does not establish deterministic safety.
Q3_ai_filled: The AI assistant drafted and revised experiment code, adversarial regression tests, statistical summaries, matched comparator design, lab harness, documentation, theory notes, and manuscript wording under the founder-selected research problem.

Task readers, numerical tolerances, split protocol, floors, observable feature map, log-linear error-shape model, stress conditions, comparator candidate grid, calibration-only comparator risk rule, and seed schemes were AI-assisted design choices and are disclosed as such.

The admissible-completion-set, task-reader-image, robust-verdict, trajectory-nonconformity, calibrated-envelope, certificate-hitting-time, and coverage-to-task equations are NEW project definitions/derivations, not existing Toledo equations.
Split conformal prediction, calibrated pose uncertainty, task-aware perception, and estimator-side early stopping are external prior art and are not claimed as inventions of this project.
Q4_assumed: Generated asymmetric point clouds and damped ICP/Kabsch are a useful numerical fixture for testing stopping logic but are not assumed to model all real pose-estimation failures.
The learned observable error-shape model is frozen after TRAIN and is not assumed optimal or transferable to real backends.
Split-conformal marginal coverage is interpreted only under the declared exchangeability assumptions; shifted conditions receive no silent transferred guarantee.
The declared box/L1 numerical readers are treated as the outcome definition only for the numerical fixture and are not assumed to guarantee physical manipulation success.

The post-review matched comparator tuning uses calibration-only unsafe-event upper bounds as a common numerical risk screen; this design is not claimed to be the unique or optimal comparator-selection procedure.
The ten-cycle study is assumed informative only about its reduced configuration and numerical generator, not the first full final-test configuration.
Trajectory-prefix timing is treated as descriptive counterfactual cost, not direct online-policy latency.
Q5_tested: I4: GitHub Actions reruns unit/adversarial controls and numerical experiments on Linux, macOS, and Windows.
I4: the split-conformal implementation uses the augmented +infinity order statistic when the required rank is n+1; the n=2, alpha=0.1 counterexample is a regression test.
I4: NaN, non-finite model state, malformed tolerances, overflow, and unbounded calibration fail closed and cannot silently create a zero-width ACT certificate.
I4: a one-episode paired equality cannot certify a 5 percentage-point non-inferiority margin; predeclared minimum test size is mechanically enforced in the lab harness.
I4: hidden ground-truth pose is absent from online learned-gate and lab-gate function signatures and is used only for offline training/calibration/evaluation.
I4: TRAIN/CALIBRATION/TEST identifiers and retired development seeds are mechanically role-separated.
I4: matched comparator parameters are selected on calibration data before new comparison-test seeds are evaluated; test outcomes are not used for tuning in the script.
I4: unsafe_act_on_covered_episode_count is required to be zero for the implemented matching numerical readers.
I4: the repeated-cycle artifact is explicitly marked reduced configuration and is mechanically checked not to claim identity with the first full standard configuration.
I4: trajectory-prefix outputs are mechanically prevented from emitting a latency-reduction PASS in the default university-lab mode.
I5 external independent human replication has not yet been obtained.

claims.executed_numerical: Coverage-qualified task stopping is executable on a public iterative rigid-registration fixture with explicit TRAIN/CALIBRATION/TEST lineage and fail-closed certificate boundaries.
claims.negative_raw_proxy_ablation: The frozen raw-proxy conformal envelope achieved 95.83% whole-trajectory coverage but HOLD 100% for all tasks, showing that coverage alone is not operational usefulness.
claims.executed_learned_certificate: In the first frozen 120-episode learned-shape final test, certificate-before-estimator occurred in 87.5-90.0% of all assigned episodes, completion differed from estimator stopping by 0 to -2.5 percentage points, observed unsafe ACT was zero, and whole-trajectory coverage was 85% against a nominal 90% target.
claims.executed_matched_comparison: On 120 new matched numerical test episodes, the trajectory-conformal certificate was not always the earliest method; relative to a learned scalar threshold it stopped later but generally showed lower observed unsafe ACT, and for keyed insertion matched estimator-default completion while trading unsafe ACT for HOLD at an earlier mean endpoint.
claims.executed_reduced_replication: Ten repeated cycles produced mean realized coverage 91.17% only under the reduced 80/80/60, K=16, 80-point configuration; this does not estimate repeated coverage of the first 160/160/120, K=20, 120-point experiment.
claims.open_hypothesis: A real iterative 6D pose backend can realize calibrated task certificates early enough to reduce directly measured online-policy latency while satisfying a predeclared task-completion non-inferiority criterion.
hold: Deterministic safety guarantee from conformal marginal coverage
Universal claim that every realized test set will achieve nominal coverage
Universal superiority over scalar thresholds or other baselines
